responseText: {"title":"Dark Mass, Small Light","question":"How much of a face can disappear into shadow before recognition fails?","introduction":"Sixteen works line this gallery, each asking the same quiet question from a different angle. Some faces press close and warm; others retreat behind dark washes, dense line-work, or near-total blackness. A few hold on by a single bright accent — a yellow bar, a tooth row, a blue iris. The exhibition traces that slow disappearance and asks where recognition ends and something else begins.","closing":"Each work tests a different threshold. By the final room, the question is no longer whether a face is present, but whether the small light that remains is enough to hold it together.","chapters":[{"title":"Surface and Presence","introduction":"Four faces where the form is still largely readable — but the surface already resists easy description, layered with marks that complicate what lies beneath.","stops":[{"slot":"W026","whyHere":"Warm amber washes and a web of black lines keep the face legible while the near-black background begins the gallery's slow withdrawal of light.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W101","whyHere":"Soft overlapping circles dissolve the background into pale gold; two blue irises hold steady as the only cool, fixed points in a warm haze.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W026 uses a dark surround to press the face forward, here the background glows softly, yet the downward tilt creates a similar sense of guarded distance."},{"slot":"W046","whyHere":"Dense overlapping lines replace tonal modelling; dark-red eye hollows pull inward while translucent circles push the surrounding space outward simultaneously.","transitionFromPrevious":"The blue irises of the previous work gave a clear focal point; here the eye positions are voids, and attention scatters across the layered surface instead."},{"slot":"W124","whyHere":"Muted teal and rust diagonal bands hold the face in place; a burst of gold and blue at the crown is the one point where the image releases pressure.","transitionFromPrevious":"W046's muted lavender-grey palette gives way to teal and rust bands, but both works share a compressed, downward-cast quality that withholds direct engagement."}]},{"title":"Line Against Dark","introduction":"Four works where darkness has claimed most of the surface and drawn lines — rather than tonal light — carry the burden of keeping a face present.","stops":[{"slot":"W084","whyHere":"Horizontal dark-blue-grey washes cover most of the face; orange lines trace structure without filling it, leaving the form open to the pale ground behind.","transitionFromPrevious":"W124's diagonal bands were muted but still colourful; here the wash is heavier and cooler, and the face begins to recede rather than hold its ground."},{"slot":"W039","whyHere":"White lines cross cheekbone and jaw while cool blue and warm red fields pull against each other; the face tilts downward into shadow at its lower edge.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works use line to describe structure over a dark field, but W039 introduces competing warm and cool grounds that create tension W084's quieter palette avoids."},{"slot":"W093","whyHere":"Black eye sockets read as pure absence; white scribble lines layer over olive-grey skin like static, while a rigid geometric net below presses against the softness above.","transitionFromPrevious":"W039's unresolved edges dissolve into ground; W093 replaces that softness with a hard diagrammatic shape at the bottom, making the collision between systems visible."},{"slot":"W065","whyHere":"A long black face hangs inside a heavy arch of hair-like loops; white lines pick out drooping eyes and four elongated teeth, leaving most of the interior empty.","transitionFromPrevious":"W093's geometric net imposed an external system on the face; here the surrounding hair-arch is organic but equally enclosing, and the interior is even more stripped back."}]},{"title":"Noise and Pressure","introduction":"Three works where the face is buried under dense, competing mark-making — the question of recognition shifts from shadow to sheer visual overload.","stops":[{"slot":"W092","whyHere":"Crimson borders press inward while yellow-green and blue threads pull outward; two red rectangles act as anchors inside a surface that reads as continuous agitation.","transitionFromPrevious":"W065's sparse white lines on black gave the face room to breathe; W092 fills every plane with crossing colour, replacing emptiness with relentless accumulation."},{"slot":"W004","whyHere":"Black-outlined panels lock together like a cracked shell; fanned white lines below and scribbled colour at the crown create tension between containment and exposure.","transitionFromPrevious":"W092's marks spread across an open white ground; W004 compresses the same density into a sealed dark form on warm brown, making the pressure feel structural rather than scattered."},{"slot":"W088","whyHere":"A dark mass dominates the frame; red, orange, and yellow-green lines gather thickest at brow and mouth, reading as friction rather than description of features.","transitionFromPrevious":"W004's armour-like panels give the dark form a hard edge; W088's dark mass has no such boundary — warm lines push back against it from within, with no clear resolution."}]},{"title":"Skull Logic","introduction":"Three works that strip the face back to its most reduced vocabulary — sockets, teeth, and outline — testing how little structure recognition actually requires.","stops":[{"slot":"W122","whyHere":"Eye sockets are dark holes; the jaw is a cage of white verticals on red; orange lines overshoot the form rather than containing it, giving the structure a restless quality.","transitionFromPrevious":"W088's dark mass was built up from layered marks; W122 strips away that density, leaving only outline and void — the face as hollow architecture."},{"slot":"W105","whyHere":"White patches assemble a skull-like face against pure black; repeated tooth loops make the grin feel insistent rather than fixed, holding the image between confrontation and dark comedy.","transitionFromPrevious":"W122's skull sits on a warm amber ground with looping orange lines; W105 removes all warmth — black ground, white patches only — making the reduction absolute."},{"slot":"W058","whyHere":"The face pushes outward rather than receding: white cross marks and a bold tooth row hold the eye at the surface, a structural contrast to the preceding skull works.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both W105 and W058 foreground teeth as a primary feature, but where W105 recedes into black, W058 presses forward with layered colour and asymmetric eye zones."}]},{"title":"The Last Light","introduction":"Two works where darkness has swallowed most of the form and a single small accent — yellow bars, white teeth — is all that holds the face together.","stops":[{"slot":"W126","whyHere":"Blue scribble-work covers the upper dome; two yellow-gold bars in near-black eye sockets and three small white teeth below are the only warm light in a cold, shadowed mass.","transitionFromPrevious":"W058's face pushed outward with dense colour; W126 reverses that entirely — darkness claims the bulk of the form and only two small yellow bars remain as evidence of a face."},{"slot":"W104","whyHere":"A tilted block floats in open teal space; the white spiral-and-cross and a cluster of white vertical bars are the only clear focal points inside dense hatching — an honest outlier that tests the gallery's question from a non-figurative angle.","transitionFromPrevious":"W126 holds recognition through two yellow bars in deep shadow; W104 offers a different kind of minimal anchor — white marks inside dense line-work — but the surrounding darkness of the teal ground echoes the same question of what little is enough."}]}]}
